Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller version of the same task. To keep from repeating forever, every recursive function must have a "base case," which is a specific condition that tells it when to stop. You can picture it like opening a set of Russian nesting dolls, where you continue opening smaller dolls until you finally reach the tiny, solid one inside. Once that simplest case is reached, the results are passed back up through each layer to build the final answer.
